findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed 6 cans in the back dry storage with severe dents along the seams (top/bottom) and sides. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the cans. PIC and Inspector discussed what types of dents to look for that should indicate a can should be rejected: major dents on the seams (top, bottom, side seam), and severe dents that indicate crushing or formation of sharp points. Ensure that cans that are received dented are rejected. Cans that are damaged during service can be used if repackaged immediately.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed ground beef stored over whole beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC had staff move the whole beef above the ground beef, following proper storage order by final cooking temperature. Ensure food is stored with ready-to-eat foods on top (no additional cooking required), followed by raw animal proteins that require cooking on the bottom. For animal proteins, the higher shelf would include fish and eggs (135-145 F final cooking temperature), stored over whole intact beef and pork (145 F), stored over ground “comminuted” beef and pork (155 F), stored over chicken and poultry of any kind on the bottom shelf (165 F). Foods with different final cooking temperatures can be stored side-by-side as long as they are in protective packaging that keeps them separate.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the dish machine was tested at less than 50ppm (Chlorine). CORRECTED: The machine was cycled several times and still tested below 50ppm. A service technician was contacted during the visit. The machine was later adjusted and tested at 50ppm (Chlorine) to correct the violation. Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly, at least 50ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: At least five to ten fruit flies were observed on the mesh bags of whole onions in the back kitchen area. The person-in-charge mentioned that the onions are usually used within a week and never are stored for long periods of time. Discussed possibly storing onions in clean trash containers or any type of sealed container to prevent attracting insects. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination and unwanted insects.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine was tested at 0ppm (CL). The machine was cycled several times and still tested at 0ppm. A service technician was contacted during the visit. The machine was later repaired and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were several insect glue traps stored above food prep areas throughout the kitchen area. The traps were filled with dead insects. Discussed and shown to the person-in-charge (PIC). Be sure to remove glue traps from above food prep areas to prevent contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the shelves holding clean dishes (green shelving near the ice machine) have an accumulation of dust, grease, and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. The inspector suggests increasing the frequency of cleaning. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the bar hand washing sink did not have soap when the inspector arrived. The PIC provided the hand sink with soap during the inspection. Ensure that every hand washing sink always has soap available for the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw meat stored over onions and cooked food in the walk-in cooler. An employee moved the raw meat below the ready-to-eat foods during the inspection. Ensure that food is stored according to the proper storage order to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the steam table was not holding foods at 135F or higher when the inspector arrived. The internal temperature of beans was 120F, queso was 125F, and rice was 120F. An employee turned up the temperature of the steam table during the inspection. When the inspector re-checked the temperatures the internal temperature of the queso was 135F and beans was 140F. The PIC was reminded that temperatures must be checked on a regular basis using a probe thermometer. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop being stored on a shelf amongst clean dishes with the handle resting on a clean lids. The lids were removed from service and placed by the dish machine for cleaning. Ensure that the ice scoop is stored in a position that does not pose a health hazard. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always cleaned when contamination occurs. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed food being stored in boxes on the floor of the walk-in freezer. Food must always be stored at least 6-inches above the floor to protect it from contamination. Ensure that the foods are moved off the floor in the walk-in freezer.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.
